question: What is the prevalence of parasitic infections in US adults?
refined_question: Among noninstitutionalized US participants in NHANES 2011-2012 (Age >=18 years), what is the survey-weighted prevalence of parasitic infection (measured serologies) (positive for Toxocara (SSTCAR = 1) or Toxoplasma IgG (>=33 IU/mL) in the 2011-2012 surplus-specimen subsample), overall and by sex, age group, race and ethnicity, and born in the united states?
title: Prevalence of Parasitic Infection (Measured Serologies) Among US Adults: A Cross-Sectional Analysis of NHANES 2011-2012
hypothesis: Parasitic infection (measured serologies) is common in this population and varies by sex, age group, race and ethnicity, and born in the united states.

pico.population: noninstitutionalized US participants in NHANES 2011-2012 (Age >=18 years)
pico.exposure: Not applicable (descriptive prevalence); subgroups: Sex, Age group, Race and ethnicity, and Born in the United States
pico.outcome: Any measured parasite seropositivity - Toxocara or Toxoplasma IgG (2011-2012)
pico.covariates: Sex, Age group, Race and ethnicity, Born in the United States, and Income-to-poverty ratio

outcome.label: Any measured parasite seropositivity - Toxocara or Toxoplasma IgG (2011-2012)

model.rationale: Prevalence estimand: survey-weighted proportions with Korn-Graubard (beta) 95% CIs, overall and by subgroup, assessed against NCHS presentation standards; population counts from weighted totals. Adjusted correlates are estimated with survey-weighted quasi-Poisson regression (prevalence ratios).

missing_data.rationale: Complete-case primary analysis within the design; multiple imputation by chained equations as sensitivity analysis when covariates are missing.

rationale.statistician: Prevalence estimand: survey-weighted proportions with Korn-Graubard (beta) 95% CIs, overall and by subgroup, assessed against NCHS presentation standards; population counts from weighted totals. Adjusted correlates are estimated with survey-weighted quasi-Poisson regression (prevalence ratios).
rationale.epidemiologist: Correlates model includes Age, Sex, Race and ethnicity, Income-to-poverty ratio, and Born in the United States to describe independent associations with any measured parasite seropositivity - toxocara or toxoplasma IgG (2011-2012); these are descriptive, not causal, contrasts. Variables on the causal pathway or sharing laboratory components with the outcome/exposure are excluded to avoid over-adjustment.

limitations: Cross-sectional design: temporality cannot be established and associations must not be interpreted causally.
Single measurement of laboratory values; within-person variability and chronicity cannot be assessed.
Residual confounding by unmeasured or imperfectly measured factors (e.g., diet, medications, menstrual blood loss).
Self-reported comorbidities and behaviours are subject to recall and social-desirability bias.
NHANES excludes institutionalized and active-duty military populations.

Operational definition (Toxocara or T. gondii IgG+): NHANES measures only selected parasites by serology (Toxocara, Toxoplasma; Trichomonas and Cryptosporidium in limited cycles). Intestinal helminths, stool ova and parasites, malaria and Strongyloides are not measured.
Operational definition (Toxocara or T. gondii IgG+): Composite is defined only where both tests were run on the same specimens (2011-2012).
